{{Short description|Simpler variant of the Riemann zeta function}}
{{One source|date=September 2025}}[[Image:Riemann Xi cplot.svg|right|thumb|300px|Riemann xi function <math> \xi(s) </math> in the [[complex plane]]. The color of a point <math> s </math> encodes the value of the function. Darker colors denote values closer to zero and hue encodes the value's [[complex number|argument]].]]

In [[mathematics]], the '''Riemann xi function''' is a variant of the [[Riemann zeta function]], and is defined so as to have a particularly simple [[functional equation]]. The function is named in honour of [[Bernhard Riemann]].

== Definition ==
Riemann's original lower-case "xi"-function, <math>\xi</math> was renamed with a <math>\Xi</math> ([[Xi (letter)|Greek uppercase letter "xi"]]) by [[Edmund Landau]]. Landau's <math>\xi</math> (lower-case "xi") is defined as<ref name=Landau1909>{{cite book |author-link=Edmund Landau |first=Edmund |last=Landau |title=Handbuch der Lehre von der Verteilung der Primzahlen |trans-title=Handbook of the Study of Distribution of the Prime Numbers <!-- |orig-publisher=Teubner |orig-location=Leipzig --> |orig-year=1909 |edition=Third |publisher=Chelsea |location=New York |year=1974 |at=§70-71 and page 894}}</ref>  
: <math>\xi(s) = \frac{1}{2} s(s-1) \pi^{-s/2} \Gamma\left(\frac{s}{2}\right) \zeta(s)</math>
for <math>s \in \mathbb{C}</math>. Here <math>\zeta(s)</math> denotes the [[Riemann zeta function]] and <math>\Gamma(s)</math> is the [[gamma function]]. 

The functional equation (or [[reflection formula]]) for Landau's <math>\xi</math> is
: <math>\xi(1-s) = \xi(s) .</math> 
Riemann's original function, renamed as the upper-case <math>\Xi</math> by Landau,<ref name=Landau1909/> satisfies 
: <math>\Xi(z) = \xi \left(\tfrac{1}{2} + z i \right) ,</math>
and obeys the functional equation
: <math>\Xi(-z) = \Xi(z) .</math>
Both functions are [[Entire function|entire]] and purely real for real arguments.

== Values ==
The general form for positive even integers is
: <math>\xi(2n) = (-1)^{n+1}\frac{n!}{(2n)!}B_{2n}2^{2n-1}\pi^{n}(2n-1)</math>
where <math>B_n</math> denotes the {{tmath|n}}th [[Bernoulli number]]. For example:
: <math>\xi(2) = {\frac{\pi}{6}} </math>

== Series representations ==
The <math>\xi</math> function has the series expansion
: <math>\frac{d}{dz} \ln \xi \left(\frac{-z}{1-z}\right) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \lambda_{n+1} z^n,</math>
where
: <math>\lambda_n = \frac{1}{(n-1)!} \left. \frac{d^n}{ds^n} 
\left[s^{n-1} \log \xi(s) \right] \right|_{s=1} = \sum_{\rho} \left[ 1- \left(1-\frac{1}{\rho}\right)^n \right],</math>
where the sum extends over <math>\rho</math>, the non-trivial zeros of the zeta function, in order of <math>\vert\Im(\rho)\vert</math>.

This expansion plays a particularly important role in [[Li's criterion]], which states that the [[Riemann hypothesis]] is equivalent to having <math>\lambda_n > 0</math> for all positive <math>n</math>.

== Hadamard product ==
A simple [[infinite product]] expansion is
: <math>\xi(s) = \frac12 \prod_\rho \left(1 - \frac{s}{\rho} \right),</math>
where <math>\rho</math> ranges over the roots of <math>\xi</math>.

To ensure convergence in the expansion, the product should be taken over "matching pairs" of zeroes, i.e., the factors for a pair of zeroes of the form <math>\rho</math> and <math>\bar\rho</math> should be grouped together.
